{{Quote|You'll never leave here. Nar Shaddaa will be your grave!|The Gran threatens Kyle Katarn|translated=1|audio=NarShadGranHunterNeverLeavehere.flac|<ref name="DF2" />}}
A '''Gran''' [[Gender/Legends|male]] who worked as a [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]] and a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] once pursued a [[Unidentified weapons smuggler|weapons smuggler]] into [[Coruscant sector/Legends|territory]] controlled by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], only to chance a run-in with [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] agent [[Kyle Katarn]]. The encounter resulted in Katarn delivering a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] injury to the [[Gran/Legends|Gran's]] [[Limb/Legends|leg]] before taking out the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] operation himself. The Gran, whose wound took three [[Standard month/Legends|months]] to heal, never forgot the debacle, leaving him with a taste for vengeance.

In [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], the [[Model 88-series administration droid|droid]] [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]] [[8t88/Legends|8t88]] hired the Gran to serve as backup during a [[Mission to Nar Shaddaa (5 ABY)|meeting]] with Katarn at the [[Rimmer's Rest/Legends|Rimmer's Rest]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], where 8t88 planned to divulge information regarding the [[Subjugation of Sulon|death]] of Katarn's [[Morgan Katarn|father]]. However, the [[Administrative droid|droid]] double-crossed Katarn and left the Gran and another [[Unidentified bounty hunter (Rimmer's Rest)|hireling]] to [[Death/Legends|kill]] him, with the Gran being particularly pleased at the prospect of a rematch. However, Katarn disarmed both hirelings before they could shoot him and then killed the Gran with his [[Bryar pistol/Legends|Bryar pistol]].

==Biography==
===Gran with a grudge===
{{Quote|I was a bodyguard looking for a smuggler a few years back. He was running weapons into the Imperial sector until you dumped his operation down a blackhole&mdash;and gave me a laser shot in the leg doing it.|The Gran recounts his first encounter with Kyle Katarn|audio=Gran-LookingForASmuggle.flac|<ref name="AudioD" />}}
[[File:A_Gran_holds_up_Kyle.png|thumb|left|250px|The Gran turns his blaster rifle on Kyle Katarn.]]
A [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] worked as a [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]]<ref name="AudioD" /> during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].<ref name="RA" /> At one point, he<ref name="RA" /> went in search of a [[Unidentified weapons smuggler|weapons smuggler]] whose operation extended into the [[Coruscant sector/Legends|Imperial sector]]. During the search, the Gran instead encountered Rebel agent [[Kyle Katarn]] and sustained a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] injury to the [[Limb/Legends|leg]], while Katarn dismantled the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] operation by himself. The Gran's wound took three [[Standard month/Legends|months]] to heal, and he held onto a grudge against Katarn.<ref name="AudioD" /> By [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]],<ref name="Date" /> the Gran was working out of the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]].<ref name="RA" />

Later that same [[Standard year/Legends|year]],<ref name="Date" /> a [[Model 88-series administration droid|droid]] [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]] named [[8t88/Legends|8t88]], working for the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]], [[Mission to Nar Shaddaa (5 ABY)|journeyed to Nar Shaddaa]] having arranged a meeting with [[Kyle Katarn]], but his aim was to obtain some information. In case Katarn refused to comply, 8t88 attempted to hire the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] to serve as a bodyguard. However, Fett declined, which forced 8t88 to find less competent backup, including the Gran and a [[Unidentified bounty hunter (Rimmer's Rest)|second bounty hunter]],<ref name="RA" /> a [[Grave Tuskens|Grave Tusken]].<ref name="DF2" />

===Rematch with Katarn===
{{Quote|Remember me? It took three months for that blaster burn to heal.''"<br />"''Can't say that I do, but the streets are filled with trash &mdash; and it's hard to tell one piece from another.|The Gran and Kyle Katarn|<ref name="RA" />}}
Arriving at Katarn's table inside the [[Rimmer's Rest/Legends|Rimmer's Rest]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]], the agent expected the droid to divulge information concerning [[Morgan Katarn|his father's]] death. Indeed, 8t88 informed Katarn of Jerec's responsibility for Morgan's [[Death/Legends|death]] during the [[Subjugation of Sulon]], as well as the Dark [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi's]] plans for the rebirth of the Empire.<ref name="DF2" /> While late to the confrontation, much to 8t88's annoyance,<ref name="RA" /> the Gran and the second bounty hunter then moved in around Katarn, leveling their blasters at him and confiscating his. The Gran warned Katarn not to move, quipping that he would look pretty funny with his head blown off.<ref name="AudioD" />

[[File:Katarn_meets_8t88.jpg|thumb|right|180px|The Gran (background) reinforces 8t88 at the Rimmer's Rest cantina.]]
8t88 then brought up the topic of having obtained a [[Hologram disc/Legends|holodisc]] from the [[Katarn family compound|home]] on the moon [[Sulon/Legends|Sulon]], which belonged to Katarn's [[Parent/Legends|father]]. Unable to access the disc's contents due to its encryption, 8t88 attempted to force help from Katarn, which was the actual reason for luring him there. Katarn refused to answer the [[Administrative droid|droid's]] questions despite being threatened with the Gran and the [[Grave Tuskens|Grave Tusken]] blasting him.<ref name="DF2" /> Seeing that Katarn would be of no help, 8t88 departed, leaving his hirelings behind to kill Katarn while offering them a hundred [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] for every body part they brought back to him.<ref name="AudioD" />

Instead of immediately shooting Katarn, the Gran took the vacated seat across the table from him and asked the Rebel agent if he remembered him from their past encounter. After Katarn retorted that he did not, the Gran began lamenting his old blaster burn, which gave Katarn the opportunity to strike.<ref name="RA" /> In one swift move, he deftly threw the Grave Tusken over his shoulder and confiscated that bounty hunter's [[DH-17 blaster pistol/Legends|DH-17 blaster pistol]], which he pointed directly at the Gran,<ref name="DF2" /> who had dropped his own weapon in the melee.<ref name="AudioD" /> Katarn then called on [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to [[Telekinesis/Legends|retrieve]] his own [[Bryar pistol/Legends|blaster]], which slid into his hand,<ref name="RA" /> much to the bewilderment of the two bounty hunters.<ref name="AudioD" />

The Gran and his partner watched as Katarn slid out from the table and began to back away. Katarn explained to them that he was going after 8t88 before mockingly adding that they should go out for lunch sometime.<ref name="RA" /> The Gran then retrieved his [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|E-11 blaster rifle]], quickly exited the room,<ref name="DF2OSG">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II: The Official Strategy Guide]]''</ref> and began running toward the main bar area.<ref name="DF2" /> However, Katarn used his Bryar [[Blaster pistol/Legends|pistol]] to shoot and kill the Gran while making his way out of the cantina and then collected the dead bounty hunter's [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]]. After Katarn killed a second Gran near the bar,<ref name="DF2OSG" /> the cantina's [[Timmy|bartender]] demanded that he leave.<ref name="DF2" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Tell me what it is, and these gentlemen won't have to indulge their darker side.|8t88 threatens Kyle Katarn with his hirelings|audio=8t88DarkSide.flac|<ref name="AudioD" />}}
[[File:Kyle_Shoots_the_Gran.png|thumb|left|250px|The Gran was gunned down by Katarn on Nar Shaddaa.]]
The Gran carried a grudge against Kyle Katarn after sustaining a long-lasting blaster injury in a prior confrontation with him.<ref name="RA" /> During their second meeting on Nar Shaddaa years later, the Gran relished holding his nemesis at gunpoint. He took the moment to question whether Katarn remembered him, which only resulted in Katarn likening him to common street trash while providing the Rebel agent with the opportunity to make his escape.<ref name="AudioD" /> The Gran cockily remarked that Nar Shaddaa would become Katarn's grave<ref name="DF2" /> before being gunned down himself only moments later.<ref name="DF2OSG" />

8t88 considered the Gran and his partner to be idiots for showing up late to the confrontation with Katarn,<ref name="RA" /> though the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] granted that they had performed well enough in taking him at gunpoint, even if they were not as skilled as Boba Fett. Nonetheless, 8t88 lacked faith in the Gran's biological intelligence,<ref name="AudioD" /> which he considered inferior to his own droid abilities.<ref name="RA" />

The Gran had [[Color/Legends|beige]] skin and purple [[Eye/Legends|eyes]],<ref name="DF2" /> which were [[Blood/Legends|bloodshot]] during his second confrontation with Katarn at the Rimmer's Rest cantina. He had a voice that sounded like a gravel crusher stuck in low gear<ref name="RA" /> and could speak both an [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Language/Legends|language]]<ref name="DF2" /> and [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]].<ref name="AudioD" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|My&hellip; My blaster! I lost my blaster!''"<br />"''There it is!|The Gran and the Grave Tusken after being disarmed by Kyle Katarn|audio=Gran-ILostMyBlaster.flac|<ref name="AudioD" />}}
The Gran armed himself with an E-11 blaster rifle during his second confrontation with Kyle Katarn on Nar Shaddaa. He also wore dark-gray [[Clothing/Legends|fatigues]] around his torso as well as black pants with a dark-gray [[Belt/Legends|belt]] and dark-gray [[Boot/Legends|boots]].<ref name="DF2" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Notable appearances===
The Gran first appeared in the [[1997]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]'' as one of two bounty hunters who accompany 8t88 while confronting Kyle Katarn on Nar Shaddaa in the game's opening cutscene. Two actors are credited as playing the bounty-hunter characters in that cutscene: [[Dan Bloom]] and [[Dylan Haggerty]], who are listed as "Bounty Hunter 1" and "Bounty Hunter 2," respectively.<ref name="DF2" />

The Gran's spoken line in that cutscene, which is translated via caption as "You'll never leave here. Nar Shaddaa will be your grave!," is actually two different "wake up" sound effects that other Gran characters emit when first sighting the player character on Nar Shaddaa. This sound effect is also repeated by other Gran characters in the ''Dark Forces II'' levels on Sulon.<ref name="DF2" />

In addition to ''Dark Forces II'', the Gran also appeared in the game's [[1998]] novella adaption ''[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent]]'', written by [[William C. Dietz]], illustrated by [[Ezra Tucker]], and published in tandem by [[Dark Horse Comics]] and [[Berkley Boulevard]];<ref name="RA" /> as well as the [[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent (audio drama)|''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' audio drama]] from author [[John Whitman]]. In accordance with 8t88's dialogue in the game, the Gran was voiced by [[Tom Keith]] in the audio drama and is credited there as "Goon 1." These stories briefly expanded on the character's backstory with Kyle Katarn.<ref name="AudioD" />

===Inconsistencies===
{{Quote|You'll never leave here alive. Nar Shaddaa will be your grave!|The Gran's differing dialogue from the ''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' novella|<ref name="RA" />}}
The scene in which the Gran confronts Kyle Katarn on Nar Shaddaa varies in detail and dialogue between the ''Dark Forces II'' video game, the ''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' novella, and the ''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' audio drama.<ref name="DF2" /><ref name="AudioD" /><ref name="RA" /> In the video game, the Gran speaks one line of dialogue before Katarn makes his escape,<ref name="DF2" /> whereas the exchange between the Gran and Katarn is significantly expanded in the two ''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' adaptations.<ref name="AudioD" /><ref name="RA" /> In particular, the novel vaguely mentions the Gran's background history with Katarn while the audio drama expounds the details of their previous encounterprior to meeting again on Nar Shaddaa.<ref name="AudioD" />

[[File:DF_Gran_Merc.png|thumb|right|250px|The confrontation between the Gran and Kyle Katarn plays out very differently between the ''Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II'' video game and its ''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' adaptations. Here, Katarn holds the Gran at gunpoint in the video-game cutscene.]]
Additionally, the manner in which Katarn executes his escape from the Gran and his partner varies, with the ''Rebel Agent'' adaptations presenting a much more frantic skirmish between the bounty hunters and Katarn.<ref name="AudioD" /><ref name="RA" /> The audio drama uniquely features punching and laser-blast sound effects before the Gran loses his blaster, which Katarn then calls to his hand with the Force;<ref name="AudioD" /> alternatively, the novella suggests that Katarn uses the Force to retrieve his confiscated Bryar pistol.<ref name="RA" /> None of these details are present in the video-game cutscene, which instead shows Katarn pointing the second bounty hunter's DH-17 blaster pistol at the Gran.<ref name="DF2" /> This article attempts to reconcile and incorporate details from all three versions, while treating the ''Dark Forces II'' video game as the highest canon source.

The Gran speaks an alien language in the video game,<ref name="DF2" /> while he speaks Basic in the novella and audio drama.<ref name="AudioD" /><ref name="RA" /> This article asserts that the Gran speaks both languages, in accordance with each of these sources.

Finally, the video game presents the player with the option of killing the Gran or leaving him alive before exiting the cantina.<ref name="DF2" /> The ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II: The Official Strategy Guide]]'', written by [[Rick Barba]], specifically directs the player to shoot the Gran, either in the booth where the level begins or in the bar, as the Gran will be waiting to attack the player.<ref name="DF2OSG" />
